div.head: Ps Cn for 25
div.ab: Si uero occiderit, amittat liberalis scutum liberalitatis; si sit illiberalis, careat libertate, si seruus uita.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 624 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: But if he kills it, let the noble lose the shield of his nobility; if he is a non-noble, let him lose his freedom; if a slave, his life.

note.seg: Quodsi statt Si u. St Cii
Quodsi instead of Si u. St Cii

lanceam et gladium zählt als aller liberorum arma Hn 78, 1; dagegen den Ritterstand bezeichnet clypeus; Ducange s. v.; Brunner Dt. Rechtsg. II 418. Verf. meint, wie o. 15, Ausstossung aus dem Ritterstande; vgl. Mat. Paris. a. 1250 (ed. Luard V 95): libertatem amisit et pecunia[m] et dimissus sine incarceratione remeare

Hn 78, 1 counts lanceam et gladium as the arma of all liberi; the knightly class, on the other hand, is denoted by clypeus; Ducange s. v.; Brunner, Dt. Rechtsg. II 418. The author means, as above 15, expulsion from the knightly class; cf. Mat. Paris, a. 1250 (ed. Luard V 95): libertatem amisit et pecunia[m] et dimissus sine incarceratione remeare

vgl. Heinrichs II. Assise: nullus chaceat [seine eigenen] feras per noctem infra forestam neque extra [also auf eigenem Grunde!], ubicunque feræ [regales] frequentant, sub pena imprisonamenti unius anni ed. Stubbs Rog. Hov. II 2472. Nicht für blosse Aufstörung, sondern für captio uenationis und nur bei Zahlungsunfähigen setzt 1217 die Charta de foresta 10: iaceat in prisona annum, et [ni]si post plegios inuenire possit, abiuret regnum

cf. Henry II's Assize: nullus chaceat [his own] feras per noctem infra forestam neque extra [so on his own land!], ubicunque feræ [regales] frequentant, sub pena imprisonamenti unius anni, ed. Stubbs, Rog. Hov. II 2472. Not for mere disturbing, but for captio uenationis, and only for those unable to pay, the Charta de foresta 10 of 1217 lays down: iaceat in prisona annum, et [ni]si post plegios inuenire possit, abiuret regnum

dagegen Charta for. 1217: nullus amittat uitam uel membra pro uenatione. Verstümmelung droht Heinrichs II. Forstassise für Forstfrevel; sie ersetzte die Todesstrafe. Auch Richard I. publicirte 1198 diese Strafdrohungen nochmals (die Howden II 245 doch schon fortlässt), soll aber nach Wendover (a. 1232 = Mat. Paris. ed. Luard III 213) Abschwören des Reichs und Kerker statt Verstümmelung eingeführt haben: vielleicht eine Tendenzlüge der Magna-charta-Partei

On the other hand, Charta for. 1217: nullus amittat uitam uel membra pro uenatione. Henry II's Forest Assize threatens mutilation for forest offences; it replaced the death penalty. Richard I too published these penalties again in 1198 (which Howden II 245 nevertheless already omits), but according to Wendover (a. 1232 = Mat. Paris, ed. Luard III 213) is said to have introduced abjuration of the realm and prison instead of mutilation: perhaps a tendentious lie of the Magna Carta party

Bei hier zitiertem Math. Paris heisst libertas ‘Privileg der Immunität und Exemtion’, nicht Adelstand. — Ritter (s. d. Gl 6. a) Osbert Giffard ward 1285 im Geistlichen Gerichte Canterburys verurteilt: insigniis militaribus sit privatus; Selden Tituli honor. II 5, 38. Über scutum gentilitium und die Strafe der Entziehung der Waffen, u. a. des scutum gegen Gefolgsleute in Frankreich, s. E. Mayer Frz. Dt. Vfg. II 134. 163. — Zu libertate carere s. o. 15a

In Matthew Paris, quoted here, libertas means ‘privilege of immunity and exemption’, not noble rank. — The knight (see that word in Gl 6. a) Osbert Giffard was sentenced in 1285 in the ecclesiastical court of Canterbury: insigniis militaribus sit privatus; Selden Tituli honor. II 5, 38. On the scutum gentilitium and the penalty of taking away arms, among them the scutum, from vassals in France, see E. Mayer Frz. Dt. Vfg. II 134. 163. — On libertate carere see above 15a
